title: Core: Move save-story, docs snippets and the mock rewrite onto the new csf-tools
description:
This PR moves three core features onto the csf-tools API from #36947: saving a story from the controls panel, docs snippet values, and source maps through the `sb.mock` rewrite. It is stacked on #36947 and merges after it.

It replaces #36938, #36935 and #36937. The diff reads best one merge commit at a time:

- `f3653277322`: save-story (#36938)
- `11246a6e2dc`: docs snippet values (#36935)
- `9287baaeb4e`: source maps (#36937)
- Six fix commits from the review below
- `2fb883ffaca`: merges #36947's own review fixes, without conflicts

## Save-story moves onto `CsfObject`

The save button was the last core feature that edited story files by hand, through the first object literal in the export. That missed whole classes of stories, and some reported success without changing the file.

`updateArgsInCsfFile` finds the story with `csf.storyObject(exportName)` and writes each arg with `set(['args', key], value)` in one transaction. If one write is refused, nothing is written.

### Clearer messages

The "Failed to save story" notification showed the csf-tools message, written for API callers. It now picks a message by reason and names the story and the arg:

> Cannot save arg "a" of story A because a spread in the story could override it.

> Cannot save story Secondary because it is the same story as Primary. Save Primary instead.

The csf-tools message becomes the error's `cause`, printed in the server log.

### Compared with `next`

Now saved, where `next` refused or changed nothing:

- CSF2 stories, `() => …` or `A.bind({})`, get an `A.args = { … }` statement.
- `export { Local as Alias }` edits `Local`.
- `args` in a constant only that story uses.
- `meta.story()` becomes `meta.story({ args: { … } })`. A new story created from it keeps the args.
- `{ ...Base }` gets `args: { ...Base.args, b: 2 }` after the spread. On `next` the args went before it, so Base's args won.

Unchanged: saving `Primary` next to `export { Primary as Secondary }` works and keeps both exports. Saving `Secondary` is still refused, with a clearer message.

Now refused, where `next` reported success but the save had no effect:

- `args` in a constant that several stories share.
- `meta.story(config)` with `config` not written inline.
- `export const Secondary = Primary`.
- An arg a later spread overrides, `args` before a story-level spread, and two `args` fields.

Now refused, where `next` saved:

- A story other code writes to, such as `A.args.x = 1`: "Cannot save story A because other code in the file changes or shares the story."
- An arg shaped like an AST node with a position, and a top-level arg named `__proto__`.

### "Save as new story"

The copy is still appended as text, then edited through `CsfObject`. Both steps run in one transaction, so a refused arg takes back the copy. It first checks two things:

- The name must be free. On `next`, a taken name such as an import wrote a duplicate declaration. Now: "Cannot create story Button because the file already uses the name Button. Choose another name."
- The source must not be another name for a story. On `next`, copying `export const B = A` wrote `export const New = A;` and dropped the args. Now: "Cannot create a story from Secondary because it is the same story as Primary. Create the new story from Primary instead." This also covers `export { Primary as Secondary }`, which failed on `next` with "cannot clone Node".

The copy shows the name its export gives. Its own `name` is removed. When a spread provides the name, as in `{ ...Base }` with a named Base, the copy sets its name after the spread. `{ name: 'Nice', ...Base }` keeps "Nice", because csf-tools refuses both removing and setting a name a later spread could override. A test pins this.

Factory stories made with `A.extend({ … })` can now be copied; `next` took them for CSF2. CSF2 stories still cannot be copied. `args` nested elsewhere, such as `parameters.docs.args`, are no longer stripped.

### Visible change: layout of saved values

Users who save from the panel will see different diffs. Saved object and array values now stay on one line, unless a member spans several lines. That is the rule `set` uses everywhere. On `next` they were expanded:

```ts
// next
myObject: {
  FOO: "BAR",
},
// this PR
myObject: { FOO: "BAR" },
```

No line width is measured, so long values stay on one line too, unless Prettier breaks them. A new `args` object becomes the last field of the story instead of the first. Existing args are still replaced in place, and quoting follows the file.

## Docs snippets print values one way

React, Angular and web components each guessed how to dedent a value copied from the story file. All three now print it with `detachedTextOf` and re-indent it to the line it lands on. Objects built from member texts go through `printMembers`.

Snippets change only in whitespace and trailing commas. The review compared React snippets for 1572 repo stories against `next`. 289 changed: 256 in whitespace only, and 33 gained a trailing comma after a written-out spread, in files that use trailing commas. `SourceEditor#trailingCommas` reads that style. `reindent` now leaves blank lines empty, so writers leave no trailing whitespace.

## Source maps

`formatCsf` was typed `{ code, map } | string` for any options, so every caller cast it. It now returns `{ code, map }` with `sourceMaps: true` and `string` without it.

`rewriteSbMockImportCalls` ignored any input map, so a webpack loader chain lost the maps of earlier loaders. It now takes `{ inputSourceMap }`, composes through it, and sets `file`. An unreadable input map is skipped, not fatal. `sourcesContent` is typed `(string | null)[]`, because entries can be `null`.

The addon-docs webpack loader now sets `file` on its map. When the incoming map cannot be read, it keeps the docs enrichment instead of dropping it.

For addon and builder authors, both API changes are additive and in MIGRATION.md. They can drop the `formatCsf` cast, and a mock loader can chain its map:

```ts
const result = rewriteSbMockImportCalls(
  source,
  this.resourcePath,
  { inputSourceMap: sourceMap },
)
callback(null, result.code, result.map ?? sourceMap, meta)
```

Old calls still work, except that `file` is now set.

## How it was checked

- Full test run at `2fb883ffaca`: 4620 passed, 27 skipped, 2 todo.
- Type checks at `2fb883ffaca`: core, builder-webpack5, builder-vite, addon-docs and the CLI. Before the fixes, the review also checked react, angular-vite, web-components and addon-vitest.

#### Manual testing

1. From the repo root, create and start the sandbox. This template uses CSF factories.

   ```sh
   yarn task sandbox --template react-vite/default-ts \
     --start-from auto
   cd ../storybook-sandboxes/react-vite-default-ts
   yarn install
   yarn storybook
   ```

2. In `src/stories/Button.stories.ts`, add `export const Bare = meta.story();`. Open Example › Button › Bare, change the label and click save. The file now has `meta.story({ args: { … } })`.
3. Add `export { Bare as Other };`. Open Other, change a control and save. The notification says "Cannot save story Other because it is the same story as Bare. Save Bare instead." The file is unchanged.
4. Open Primary, change a control and choose "Create new story". Name it `Button`: the dialog says the file already uses that name. Name it `Copy`: the file gets `export const Copy = meta.story({ … })` with the panel's args.
5. Open `http://localhost:6006/manifests/components.html` and find Header › Logged In. The snippet shows `name: "Jane Doe",` 2 spaces in from `user={{`. On `next` it is 6.

## Not in this PR

- #36949, which commits a mutation only when it must.
- "Save as new" from a story exported only as `export { Local as Alias }`. It still fails with "cannot clone Node", as on `next`.
- Saving AST-shaped data with a position, or `args` before a spread that lacks `args`. Both need csf-tools changes.
- React's bound-story path and its spread for invalid prop names still build objects by hand. Vue keeps its own dedent.
- The Vite plugin's map composition, and `file` in `formatCsf`'s map.
- Dropping the casts in the rsbuild, rspack, Parcel and react-spectrum loaders.

## Review

Each part had an Opus review at high effort first. `b46cbec7fbe` and `1f91a3f873e` reconcile the merges: one drops `expand: 'multiline'`, the other moves `printObject` onto `printMembers`.

Then one Opus review at xhigh effort covered the merged diff and this description. It compared the save cases above with `next` and found no bug in save atomicity, snippets, maps or the merges. Findings and what was done:

- Medium: refused saves showed csf-tools internals. Fixed in `b7d643ca69b`, with the two "Save as new" checks.
- Low: a copy kept a name a spread provides. Fixed in `7adbd5c3c02`.
- Low: `A.extend({ … })` stories were refused as CSF2. Fixed in `e9f1e40df6d`.
- Low: `sourcesContent` was typed `string[]` but can hold `null`. Fixed in `ea4f975a349`.
- Low: the docs loader did not set `file` and lost its enrichment on an unreadable map. Fixed in `1ecbd384c3b`.
- Low, product call: saved objects lose their expanded layout. Kept, and described above.
- Nit: "Save as new" relied on a throw instead of a transaction. Fixed in `4ffb6a3b4ab`.
- Nit: some snippet objects are still built by hand. Listed above.
- Nit: `f3653277322` and `11246a6e2dc` only compile with the reconcile commit after each. Left as is; `git bisect` may need to skip them.
- Several before/after claims in the old description were wrong against `next`. This text corrects them.

 These editors share the file's change tracking and diagnostics and expose the same read and mutation methods as configs and stories.
+
+## Printing with source maps
+
+`formatCsf(csf)` returns the printed code as a string. `formatCsf(csf, { sourceMaps: true })` returns `{ code, map }`, and is typed that way, so the result needs no cast. `map` is a hi-res map from the code `loadCsf` was given to the output, with the source named `sourceFileName`, or else the file name the CSF was loaded with. When that code came from an earlier transform, pass its map, as an object or as JSON, as `inputSourceMap`: the result then maps to the original, and its sources keep the names and the content the input map gave them. An entry of `sourcesContent` is `null` for a source whose content the input map did not carry. An input map that cannot be read only costs the mapping through it: the map then goes from the loaded code, as without one, and the reason is logged at debug level.
+
+A webpack loader chains its incoming map like this, and names the module in `file`, which webpack's map type requires and `formatCsf` leaves unset:
+
+```ts
+const csf = loadCsf(content, { makeTitle, fileName: this.resourcePath }).parse();
+// Edit `csf`, for example with `enrichCsf`.
+const { code, map } = formatCsf(csf, { sourceMaps: true, inputSourceMap: sourceMap });
+callback(null, code, { ...map, file: this.resourcePath });
+```
+
+`rewriteSbMockImportCalls(code, fileName, { inputSourceMap })` in `storybook/internal/mocking-utils` maps the preview file through `inputSourceMap` the same way, also when that map cannot be read, and sets `file` to `fileName` itself. Its map is `null` when the file has no `sb.mock(import(...))` call to rewrite, so a loader passes its incoming map on in that case:
+
+```ts
+const result = rewriteSbMockImportCalls(source, this.resourcePath, { inputSourceMap: sourceMap });
+callback(null, result.code, result.map ?? sourceMap, meta);
+```
